reasoning: The LLM fidelity evaluation identified severe structural and content defects, including the pipeline getting stuck in an infinite loop causing massive duplication of list items (over 30 times) and omitting the rest of the list. Combined with 22 displaced hyperlinks, retained header/footer elements, and broken heading hierarchy, the document suffers from catastrophic structural failure and requires rejection.

concerns.description: Significant text omission within a section
concerns.analysis: On page 13, under '23) What is a communication kit?', the pipeline became stuck in an infinite loop while extracting the bulleted list under 'One-on-one communication'. Because it repeated the first few sub-bullets dozens of times, it entirely failed to extract the rest of the list content. Critical sub-bullets regarding 'Fact sheets are available at...' and the items 'Magnifying devices' and 'Flashlights' are completely missing from the output.
concerns.source_pdf_quote: o Fact sheets are available at https://www.ncdhhs.gov/dsdhh/emergencyresponders [...] Magnifying devices including those with lights for people with low vision - Flashlight or small lamp for low light vision needs
concerns.output_quote: [Text is completely absent due to repetition loop terminating early]
concerns.location: Page 13, under '23) What is a communication kit?'

concerns.analysis: The numbered questions throughout the document are all visually styled identically in the source PDF, indicating they are siblings at the same hierarchical level. However, the output assigns inconsistent heading levels to them, incorrectly nesting some under others.
concerns.source_pdf_quote: Page 5: '3) The person appears not to respond...', '4) A person has clear speech...', '5) Which tools can I use...' are all visually siblings.
concerns.output_quote: Question 3 is rendered as an H2, while Questions 4 and 5 are rendered as H3s nested under Question 3. Similar issues occur on pages 7, 8, and 10.

concerns.analysis: The HTML output contains a massive duplication of list items. The block for 'One-on-one communication' and its nested sub-items ('A box (minimum) of clear face masks...', 'Paper and black markers', etc.) from Section 23 of the source document is repeated sequentially more than 30 times in the HTML output.
